text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran another autoscale experiment on the spot-backed inference pools last night. Sharing config + observations.

kevin: nice, what changed from the previous run?

maria: Main changes:
- tightened scale-out trigger (pending_queue threshold lowered)
- shorter scale-out cooldown to reduce missed early-surge windows
- enabled a small ondemand warm pool as a fallback for interruptions

maria: Config excerpt:
```
autoscaler:
  mode: mixed-capacity
  scale_out:
    pending_queue: 3
    gpu_util_pct: 55
    sustained_seconds: 10
  cooldowns:
    scale_out: 30s
    scale_in: 5m
  surge_control:
    max_surge: 2
    surge_window: 120s
  fallback:
    ondemand_warm_pool: 3
    preemptible_fill_policy: best_effort
```

lucas: curious about that 30s scale_out cooldown — seems short for provisioning GPUs. Why 30s?

maria: We wanted earlier capacity for short-lived bursts (chat bursts). With continuous batching, warm-up is fast. 30s prevents immediate flapping but still catches quick surges. Observed better tail latency.

kevin: What about interruption noise? spikes of spot evictions can cause cascade scale-outs.

ops-bot: [alert] 2026-02-11T02:14:22Z us-west-2: 4 preemptible evictions in 15m affecting pool spot-3b.

sre-oncall: saw that. During the experiment we had 3 concurrent evictions which triggered 2 ondemand spin-ups. Latency bump ~ +12ms p95 for 10m.

anya: How expensive was the ondemand fallback? need to compare cost vs p99 latency SLA.

maria: Cost delta for the 3-node warm pool over 24h ~ +4.7% on that fleet, but p99 improved by ~18% during peak bursts. Tradeoff looks good for user-facing routes.

lucas: Did you try surge_window shorter than 120s? Might reduce over-provisioning on noisy workloads.

maria: Yeah tried 60s — less over-provisioning but missed a few very short spikes (<=30s) where requests queued. 120s is sweet spot for our workload mix.

kevin: Any change to metric sources? Are we still using gpu_util as trigger or switching to pending_queue only?

maria: We use a hybrid: pending_queue is primary to avoid scaling on cold cache CPU artifacts; gpu_util prevents scaling on single noisy worker. Combined reduced false positives.

sre-oncall: Action for next week:
- rotate preemptible availability zones for pool (reduce correlated evictions)
- add eviction rate as a soft dampener for scale_out (if eviction_rate > 0.2 then prefer ondemand_warm_pool)

anya: +1 to AZ rotation. Also suggest a short hysteresis after interruption storms: ignore scale_out triggers for 2m after >N evictions.

maria: I'll push a small PR with the surge/cooldown defaults and an optional eviction-dampener flag. Will include perf dashboard links and cost delta.

kevin: thanks — please tag me and @sre-oncall on the PR.

maria: will do. summary: mixed-capacity + small warm ondemand pool + max_surge=2 + 30s scale_out cooldown gave best tradeoff in our experiments. Next: AZ rotation + eviction dampener.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: autoscaler config v0.6 -> staging at 2026-02-12T17:00:00Z

lucas: thanks team :+1:
